clue.text: Weather protection as doctor goes round in the morning

indicators.note: the doctor's letters go round, enclosing, the morning abbreviation in this clue

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: A doctor on morning rounds carries something to keep the rain off.
explanation.walkthrough: A GAMP is a large umbrella, named after Mrs Gamp in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamp is an old British word for a big umbrella, which protects against rain.

clue.text: Refuse to boast, coming up to maturity

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to brag is to boast
age is maturity

explanation.surface: Declining to show off as one grows older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns BRAG to GARB; 'Refuse' is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is rubbish, refuse thrown away.

clue.text: Formidable woman, twice a mother

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A fearsome woman who has had two children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice a mother' looks like a woman with two children, but it gives two words for mother; the answer also reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A madam is a domineering, imperious woman.

clue.text: Become wedged, we hear, in part of doorway

indicators.note: says the word for being wedged is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to jam is to become stuck fast

explanation.surface: Something gets stuck as it is heard, in the frame of a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is an upright side post of a door frame.

clue.text: King for half a year and one short day

indicators.note: half a year means its second half of letters here

parts.note: Thur is a shortened form of Thursday, one day of the week

explanation.surface: A monarch reigning for six months and a brief day.
explanation.walkthrough: AR is the back half of YEAR; King Arthur is the legendary British king.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur was the legendary king of Camelot.

clue.text: Port or claret

definitions.meaning: a French seaport on the Garonne
claret is the British name for red wine from that region

explanation.surface: A choice of after-dinner wines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests the fortified wine, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bordeaux is a French port city, and its red wine is called claret.

clue.text: Respond to a plea to go back on stage?

definitions.meaning: to answer a request or stimulus, to respond
read as a prefix meaning again plus a word for performing, so perform once more

explanation.surface: An actor answers the audience's call to come back out for more.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as RE-ACT: to act again, as an actor might when called back.
explanation.definitionFit: Reacting is responding; acting again is performing once more on stage.

clue.text: Hitching post?

parts.note: getting hitched means marrying, so a post or place where weddings are done

explanation.surface: A rail for tethering horses.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a civil wedding takes place at the local register office, often called this.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where civil marriages are registered and conducted.

clue.text: Entry to a profession

definitions.meaning: a profession can be an avowal or confession of something

explanation.surface: Getting into a career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'profession' looks like a career, but here it is a declaration.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission means both being allowed in and an acknowledgement or confession.

clue.text: Abbey can change religion, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the pieces are said aloud to give the entry

parts.note: a tin is a can; to turn is to convert to another faith

explanation.surface: A monastery can convert its faith, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Tintern Abbey is a ruined abbey in the Wye valley, Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintern is a famous ruined Cistercian abbey in Monmouthshire.

clue.text: She leads those in retreat

parts.note: a woman heading a community of women who have withdrawn from the world

explanation.surface: A commander of a retreating army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' suggests an army falling back, but it is a religious house.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a convent of nuns.

clue.text: New cadet or old soldier

indicators.note: new tells us to make a fresh arrangement of the letters in the next words

explanation.surface: A fresh recruit or a veteran trooper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' scrambles CADET OR into REDCOAT, the old name for a British soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcoats were British soldiers of earlier centuries, named for their scarlet tunics.

clue.text: Troops failing to finish the course

indicators.note: the troops' word stops short, losing its closing letter in this clue

parts.note: a regiment is a body of troops

explanation.surface: Soldiers fall short of completing their training course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to finish' removes the final T of REGIMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of diet, exercise or treatment.

clue.text: Saul's home, woefully poor accommodation

indicators.note: woefully means badly, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Saul's dwelling is a wretched place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woefully' rearranges SAULSHOME into ALMSHOUSE; the possessive's S counts here.
explanation.definitionFit: An almshouse was charitable housing for the needy, so lodging for the poor.

clue.text: Female brought back into side is useless

indicators.note: brought back says the letters found are read in the opposite direction
into says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A woman returned to the team is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' finds EISUS inside sidE IS USeless; 'brought back' turns it to SUSIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Susie is a woman's given name, so a female.

clue.text: What's needed to quieten a more demanding audience

definitions.text: What's needed to quieten a more demanding audience

parts.words: What's needed to quieten a more demanding audience
parts.note: an audience calling for more is only settled by an extra piece performed after the end

explanation.surface: How do you calm a crowd that is getting more insistent?
explanation.definitionFit: An encore is the extra number given when an audience calls out for more.

clue.text: Cuts off credit of Chinese food-raiser

parts.note: chops means cuts off
tick is slang for credit

explanation.surface: A restaurant stops letting a Chinese diner pay later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on tick' is British slang for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A chopstick lifts food to the mouth in Chinese eating.

clue.text: One with minor responsibilities in a newspaper

definitions.meaning: someone legally responsible for a child, a minor

explanation.surface: A junior staffer with small duties at a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian looks after a child under age; The Guardian is a UK daily paper.

clue.text: Repaid exact thousand pounds in debt

indicators.note: in places the pieces for exact and the money inside the colour of debt

parts.note: to be in the red is to be in debt
even means exact, level
G, a grand, is slang for a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Paid back an exact grand while owing money.
explanation.walkthrough: R(EVEN G)ED; 'Repaid' in the sense of got even.
explanation.definitionFit: To be revenged is to have repaid an injury.

clue.text: See point in remedies for stoppages

indicators.note: in places the pieces for see and point inside the word for remedies

parts.note: cures are remedies
lo is an old word meaning see or behold
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Look for the key spot among treatments for blockages.
explanation.walkthrough: C(LO S)URES.
explanation.definitionFit: Closures are shutdowns or stoppages.

clue.text: Make tidy profit? Very much so

definitions.meaning: to make a large profit, a killing

explanation.surface: Earn a nice sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tidy profit' reads as one phrase but splits between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean up means both to tidy and to make a big financial gain.

clue.text: Where seconds do the work of a minute

definitions.text: Where seconds do the work of a minute

parts.words: Where seconds do the work of a minute
parts.note: in boxing the helpers called seconds tend their fighter during the one-minute break between rounds

explanation.surface: A puzzle about time: seconds doing a minute's job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' and 'minute' look like units of time, but the seconds are a boxer's attendants and the minute is the rest between rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's corner is the spot in the ring where his attendants work on him between rounds.

clue.text: Early caller gets egg in a roll

indicators.note: in puts the egg-shaped letter inside the word for a list

parts.note: a roster is a roll or list of names
O is egg-shaped

explanation.surface: A dawn visitor brings an egg in a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll' looks like bread, but it is a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel crows at dawn, calling early.

clue.text: Where action may involve rackets, in more ways than one

definitions.text: Where action may involve rackets, in more ways than one

parts.words: Where action may involve rackets, in more ways than one
parts.note: legal actions over criminal rackets, and play with tennis or squash rackets

explanation.surface: Places where crooked dealings lead to action.
explanation.definitionFit: Law courts try cases and tennis courts host racket sports.

clue.text: One of the sisters Lewis Carroll initiated, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak says the letters are pronounced as they are said aloud

parts.note: the initials of Lewis Carroll are L and C

explanation.surface: Lewis Carroll began a tale about one of a group of sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: In Alice in Wonderland the Dormouse tells of three sisters, Elsie, Lacie and Tillie; Elsie stands for L.C., Lorina Charlotte Liddell, Alice's elder sister.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is one of the three sisters in the Dormouse's treacle-well tale.

clue.text: Such duties come with one's position in society

definitions.text: Such duties come with one's position in society

parts.words: Such duties come with one's position in society
parts.note: some tasks are held by virtue of holding a particular office rather than by appointment

explanation.surface: Social standing brings its obligations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'position in society' suggests social rank, but it means an office held, as on a club committee.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for by virtue of office, describing duties or membership that come with a post.

clue.text: Car to handle well going round a bend

indicators.note: the coping word wraps around the bend's letter in this clue

parts.note: to cope is to handle well
a U-bend is shaped like the letter U

explanation.surface: A car managing well as it takes a corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupé is a two-door car with a fixed roof.

clue.text: Driving a point home, a point poorly presented

parts.note: N, north, is a compass point
ailing means poorly, unwell

explanation.surface: Hammering home an argument that was weakly made.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'a point' is in the definition; the second gives N, north.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailing something means hammering it in, driving the pointed nail home.

clue.text: Get someone else to do the fighting

definitions.text: Get someone else to do the fighting

parts.words: Get someone else to do the fighting
parts.note: a reading of enlisting another person for the army, to fight in your stead

explanation.surface: Avoiding a scrap by sending a substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist a new soldier is to bring someone in to fight.

clue.text: A game to settle the Ashes?

definitions.meaning: a card game played for stakes
a fireside iron rod used to stir and settle the ashes in a grate

explanation.surface: A match to decide the cricket series between England and Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the England–Australia cricket series, but here it is the fire's ashes, stirred by a fire iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker is a card game, and a poker is a metal rod for stirring a fire.

clue.text: Record is accepted by only 50% of MCC

indicators.note: accepted by says the little word goes inside the letters for the number

parts.note: MCC in Roman numerals is 1200; half of that is 600, DC

explanation.surface: A record goes only halfway to being accepted by the cricket club.
explanation.walkthrough: MCC is the Marylebone Cricket Club, cricket's governing body, but here it is read as Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record.

clue.text: Trendy clothes changed on inclination

definitions.meaning: fashionable clothing, as in slang for kit
what a cyclist or driver shifts when going up a slope

explanation.surface: Fashionable outfits altered on a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclination' looks like a whim but it is a slope, where gears get changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is slang for fashionable clothes, and gears are shifted on hills.
